reasons: Covers the token header and the patient id header in the important cases.
Does not cover the 401 refresh flow or failed requests.

terms.meaning: A fake stand-in for a real piece of code, so a test can control what it does.
A step that runs on every request or response, letting the app add or check headers in one place.
A login key sent in the request header that proves who the user is.
A person who manages health records for a family member.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Fake network library setup
sections.what: Replaces the real network library with a fake one that records the request and response steps. Also imports the API client and the auth store.
sections.why: Lets the tests check the headers without making real network calls.
sections.watch_out: The fake must keep the same shape as the real client, or the tests will stop testing real behavior.

sections.name: Web API Client & Auth Interceptors
sections.title: Header checks for each user case
sections.what: Sets sample users and tokens, then checks three cases: the token is sent, the patient id is sent for a caregiver viewing a family member, and the patient id is left out when the user is viewing their own profile.
sections.why: These are the cases that decide whose records a request reads, so they need explicit checks.
sections.watch_out: The tests read the first saved request handler. If another test adds a handler first, these tests will check the wrong one.

summary: Tests the shared web API client, checking that it adds the right login token and the patient id header for caregiver views.
purpose: Protects the rule that every request carries the signed-in user's token, and that a caregiver viewing a family member sends that member's id.
why: Wrong headers would send requests for the wrong patient or without authorization, so these checks guard against a serious privacy mistake.
how: The file replaces the real axios library with a fake that records the interceptors. It then sets up sample users in the store and calls the saved request handler directly. It checks the authorization header and the patient id header in three cases: normal user, caregiver for a family member, and a user viewing their own profile.
inputs: Sample users and tokens set in the auth store.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each case.
risks: The tests depend on the first saved request handler being the one under test, which can break if the setup order changes. The response handler, token refresh, and error handling are not tested here.
debug: If these tests fail after a change to api.ts, compare the header rules in the request handler with the expected values in each test. If the mock stops working, check that the axios mock still matches how api.ts creates the client.
